cohort: The study included 130 healthy newborns with a mean gestational age of 39 weeks and a mean birth weight of 3075g.
finding: The prevalence of cranial deformities (PDP and positional brachycephaly) was notable at birth (19.2% and 86.2% respectively) and significantly increased within the first month after birth, with deformities becoming more pronounced.
mod_finding: The mean cephalic index was significantly lower in breech fetuses, but no significant differences in cranial deformities were observed between other delivery methods.
cross-section timing: Immediately after birth (mean age 3.3 days) and at 1 month of age
